subject: Sangoma dedicated estimate: tokens/sec baseline, SLO fit, and headroom
messages:
From: Alex Nguyen <alex@sangoma.ai>

Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@sangoma.com>

Subject: Initial workload profile + target SLOs for dedicated sizing

Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for taking this on. Quick context: Sangoma's rollout plan for Q3 centers on a voice-assist & summarization feature embedded in our support console. Expected traffic profile (rough):
- Peak concurrency: 120 concurrent sessions during PST mornings (peak hour).
- Typical session: 3 inference calls (prompt + follow-ups) per conversation.
- Average tokens/request (prompt + completion): 1,100 tokens
- Target SLO: 95th percentile generation latency <= 400ms (user-facing).

We expect a 12-month commit if the economics and latency hold. Can you provide a baseline tokens/sec estimate and headroom recommendation for a Dedicated pool? Attached is a small token-profile CSV from our staging traces. Also curious how you think about caching/prefix reuse for multi-turn sessions — we expect repeated context in the first two turns.

Appreciate a quick back-of-envelope we can use in procurement and a time to sync next week.

Thanks,
Alex Nguyen
Head of Product, Sangoma AI

Subject: Re: Initial workload profile + target SLOs for dedicated sizing

Alex —

Thanks for the profile, that CSV was helpful. High-level back-of-envelope while we run a deeper sim:
- Avg tokens/request: 1,100 (as you reported). Assuming 3 calls/session and 120 concurrent sessions at peak -> ~396 concurrent live requests.
- If we budget 1,100 tokens at p95 generation latency <= 400ms, we need to translate tokens/sec per GPU for our preferred model family. For rw-medium-like configs we see ~14k tokens/sec sustained per A100-80GB GPU when serving with batching targets optimized for 350–450ms p95 under multi-turn reuse.
- Baseline sustained tokens/sec needed at peak: (120 sessions * 3 calls * 1100 tokens) / 0.4s ≈ 990,000 tokens/sec if you treated every call as serialized to the SLO window — this is conservative and assumes no batching or KV reuse. With realistic batching and KV cache reuse (prefix reuse on the first two turns), we typically observe an efficiency improvement of 6–10x on tokens/sec demand.

Prelim recommendation (conservative production shape):
- Recommended starting slab: 8 x A100-80GB GPUs dedicated (primary slab).
- Burst pool: 2 x A100-80GB for traffic surges and background rebuilds.
- Estimated sustained throughput (with batching + KV reuse): ~180k–240k tokens/sec effective capacity from primary slab.
- Safety/headroom: target 30% operational headroom for autoscaling/maintenance.

Next steps: Marissa, can you run a short sim on the attached token profile with rw-medium and a quantized rw-medium-8bit variant and share latency percentiles and tokens/sec per-GPU numbers? Ben, I'll let you drive AMP and pricing options.

Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Alex / team —

I ran the token profile through our local sim harness and attached the short write-up (sangoma_multiparty_latency_tests.md). Summary highlights and an operational sizing proposal below.

Key sim assumptions:
- Model: rw-medium (float32) and rw-medium-8bit (quantized).
- Batch targeting: dynamic batching with an affinity window tuned to 30–50ms to keep p95 under 400ms.
- KV reuse: we assume 40% token reuse across the first two turns for multi-turn sessions.
- Network + preprocessing overhead: 30–70ms depending on region.

Observations:
- rw-medium (fp32): p50/p95 per-request generation latency at avg 1,100 tokens: 120ms / 380ms when served on batch sizes that keep GPU kernels saturated. Effective tokens/sec per A100-80GB GPU (observed): ~22k tokens/sec peak, ~16k sustained under our traffic shape.
- rw-medium-8bit: p50/p95: 140ms / 420ms. Effective tokens/sec per GPU: ~28k peak, ~20k sustained. Note p95 slightly exceeds 400ms in the quantized run on worst-case single-node bursts.

Sizing recommendation (production):
- Primary Dedicated slab: 10 x A100-80GB GPUs (fp32 serving rw-medium) to comfortably meet p95 <= 400ms with 30% headroom. This yields ~160k–220k sustained tokens/sec depending on efficiency.
- Alternative cost-optimized slab: 8 x A100-80GB GPUs serving rw-medium-8bit with a canary policy that falls back to fp32 for >70% load; this reduces baseline cost but requires strict canarying because p95 slips in single-node surge scenarios.
- Burst pool: 2 x A100-80GB dedicated for short spikes and model rebuilds.
- Autoscale policy: scale out by 2 GPUs at 80% sustained slab utilization for >10 minutes; scale in after 30 minutes below 60%.

Operational notes and runbook highlights:
- Enable per-route KV caching for session-prefixed prompts to capture the 40% reuse we saw in traces; this is the single biggest savings on tokens/sec demand.
- Set per-request max_response_tokens to 1,500 to bound worst-case tail latency and protect the slab.
- Canary plan: begin with 4 GPUs in the canary subset (rw-medium-8bit) for 48 hours with shadow traffic at 10% before moving to full-8gpu baseline.

Attachments: sangoma_multiparty_latency_tests.md (detailed percentile tables), mutual-action-plan.xlsx (AMP draft).

Let me know if you'd like a follow-up call to walk through the percentile tables.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
